AuthnInviteInvitation.description: One invitation as the management face shows it. It never carries the acceptance token.

accepted_at.description: When the invitation was accepted, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; null while it has not been accepted.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC of issuance.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline in UTC; a pending invitation at or past it can no longer be accepted.

id.description: The invitation's opaque identifier, used to revoke it.

invited_by.description: The account identifier of the issuer; empty when a host command issued the invitation without an HTTP identity. During an impersonation it is the impersonated account.

invited_by_name.description: The display name of the account that issued the invitation. Absent when a host command issued it, the account no longer exists, or the account read fails; during an impersonation it is the impersonated account's name.

invited_by_username.description: The username of the account that issued the invitation. Absent when a host command issued it, the account no longer exists, the account has no username, or the account read fails; during an impersonation it is the impersonated account's username.

last_sent_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC of the most recent send. Issuance always writes it, so it is never null.

revoked_at.description: When the invitation was revoked, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC; null while it has not been revoked.

role.description: The role the invitation grants beside the membership. Absent when the invitation grants no role, never null. A resend keeps it unchanged.

send_count.description: How many times the invitation was sent: the first issuance counts as one and every resend adds one.

state.description: The state the server judges with the same clock the listing's status filter uses: pending, expired, accepted or revoked. A client shows this and never derives expiry from its own clock.

status.description: The stored state. Expiry is not stored: an expired pending invitation still reads pending.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the invitation grants a membership in.

AuthnInviteIssued.description: The answer of an issue or a resend: the invitation's view, the outcome of the notice, and the one-time acceptance token only when the notice did not reach the address.

email_delivery.description: How the acceptance notice ended: sent when the carrier accepted it, failed when delivery failed or its outcome is unknown, and not_configured when the assembly delivers no mail. A failed notice does not undo the invitation, and the token beside it is still the one-time link; a sent notice carries no token in this answer.

invitation.description: The issued invitation; a token is delivered beside it only when the notice did not reach the address.

token.description: The acceptance token, present only when email_delivery is failed or not_configured: the inviter has to hand the link over. Absent when the notice was sent, because the recipient already holds it.

AuthnInvitePage.description: One page of a tenant's invitations together with the cursor of the next page.

invitations.description: The invitations of this page, in four groups: unexpired pending, expired pending, accepted, revoked. Each group is newest first with the identifier as the tie-break. A row that crosses its deadline between pages can change group.

next_cursor.description: The cursor of the next page, empty on the last page

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: Returns one page of the tenant's invitations in four groups: unexpired pending first, then expired pending, then accepted, then revoked. Each group is ordered by creation time descending with the identifier as the tie-break, and the cursor carries the group so the next page resumes after it; a row that crosses its deadline between two pages moves to a later group and can therefore be repeated at the boundary, never skipped, because the clock only moves a row forward. The status query narrows the page: pending is a pending invitation whose deadline has not passed, expired is a pending invitation whose deadline has passed, and accepted and revoked are the terminal stored states; an absent status lists every state, and a value outside the set is refused with 400. Expiry is derived from the deadline, not stored, so an expired row still reads status pending. The cursor is opaque: pass the previous page's next_cursor as after to resume, and a cursor this build did not mint, including one in an earlier format or carrying an unknown version, is refused with 400 rather than served as the first page. A read writes no audit row.

parameters.description: Maximum number of invitations to return. Omitted or 0 serves 100; a value above 1000 is capped at 1000. A negative or non-integer value is refused with 400.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's next_cursor; omit it to start at the first page. A value this build did not mint, including one in an earlier format or carrying an unknown version, is refused with 400 rather than served as the first page.
parameters.name: after

parameters.description: Narrow the page to one view: pending is a pending invitation whose deadline has not passed, expired is a pending invitation whose deadline has passed, and accepted and revoked are the terminal stored states. Omitted lists every state. A value outside this set is refused with 400. Expiry is derived from the deadline, not stored.
parameters.name: status

parameters.description: The tenant's name the invitation belongs to. The path-tenant layer resolves it to the internal identifier before the handler runs and holds it to the tenant the request resolved to; the authn.membership.manage decision is made in that tenant.
parameters.name: tenant

post.description: Normalizes the address (trimmed, lower-cased printable ASCII with exactly one @, at most 254 bytes), then issues a pending invitation. The address cannot be a service account's, cannot already be a member of the tenant (active or suspended), and cannot already hold an unexpired pending invitation; the system tenant cannot be invited into. expires_at is optional: omitted or null takes the configured lifetime (168 hours by default); the zero instant, or a deadline not later than the current time, is refused with 400, and one later than 90 days after issuance is refused. An expired pending invitation for the same tenant and address is superseded: the old row stays expired and a new invitation takes the live slot. An optional role grants that role beside the membership: it must exist in the tenant (400 invitation-role-unknown), the caller must hold authz.tenant.role.manage, and the role must be one the caller may grant (403 invitation-role-protected for platform-admin, a permission the caller does not hold, or the host write guard's refusal). When the assembly has an invitation notifier, the acceptance notice is delivered to the address and email_delivery reports sent, failed or not_configured; a failed notice does not undo the invitation, which is still answered 201, with its one-time token only when the notice was not sent. Requires the authn.membership.manage decision in the tenant; failure to write the mandatory audit row answers 503 without issuing.

parameters.description: The tenant's name the invitation belongs to. The path-tenant layer resolves it to the internal identifier before the handler runs and holds it to the tenant the request resolved to; the authn.membership.manage decision is made in that tenant.
parameters.name: tenant

schema.description: The issue request: the invited address, which is normalized before it is stored, and an optional deadline.

email.description: The invited address as given; it is trimmed, lower-cased and must be printable ASCII with exactly one @, at most 254 bytes.

expires_at.description: Absolute deadline in RFC 3339. Omitted or null takes the configured lifetime; the zero instant, or a value not later than the current time, is refused with 400.

role.description: The role to grant beside the membership. Omitted grants no role. The role must exist in the tenant, the caller must hold authz.tenant.role.manage, every permission the role carries must be within the caller's held set, and it may not be platform-admin.

requestBody.description: The address to invite and an optional absolute deadline. Only email is required.

201.description: The invitation view and the notice outcome; the one-time token only when the notice was not sent

400.description: The body could not be read or the address is malformed (urn:speed:authn:bad-request); the deadline is the zero instant or is not later than issuance (urn:speed:authn:bad-request); the address belongs to a service account or the tenant is the system tenant (urn:speed:authn:invitation-target-invalid); the deadline lies more than 90 days after issuance (urn:speed:authn:invitation-expiry-too-long); the role is not one the tenant has (urn:speed:authn:invitation-role-unknown)

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The caller may not manage memberships in the tenant (urn:speed:authn:forbidden); The acting account holds an email address it has not proved (urn:speed:authn:contact-required); the role is platform-admin, carries a permission the caller does not hold, or the host write guard refuses the binding (urn:speed:authn:invitation-role-protected)

409.description: The address is already a member of the tenant (urn:speed:authn:invitation-member), or already holds an unexpired pending invitation (urn:speed:authn:invitation-pending)

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

delete.description: Revokes a pending invitation that has not expired and voids its token; the invitation identifier also serves as the decision's target. Revoking an already revoked invitation succeeds idempotently, while an expired or accepted one answers 409 invitation-terminal: removing a membership is not this route's job, and an expired link no longer grants anything. Failure to write the mandatory audit row answers 503 without revoking.

post.description: Resends a pending invitation that has not expired. The same row keeps its identity and its deadline; a new token replaces the old one, which stops working. send_count counts every send, the first issuance as one, and last_sent_at is the moment of the latest. The admission order is the issue route's: sign-in, the signup gate, the authn.membership.manage decision with the invitation identifier as its target, and the mandatory resend audit row on that identifier. The domain call then charges the issuing account's send budget before the terminal check, so a terminal row still costs the operator, and the address's and the deployment's budgets after it, counting those two only when the write lands. An expired, accepted or revoked invitation answers 409 invitation-terminal, and an identifier naming no invitation of the tenant is a bare 404. The notice and the one-time link follow the issue answer: sent carries no token, failed and not_configured carry one.
